rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so the table is pushed toward full coverage: BCF and FLA get the highest SecurityGain (0.9) since this binary is tiny (209 bytes of text, largest function 70 bytes) and can absorb flattening/bogus-control-flow bloat with negligible absolute runtime impact on a virtual-circle toy workload; FLA's DiversityGain is raised to 0.8 because flattening the handful of small methods (Expand, MoveTo, Hide, Show) maximally disrupts CFG-matching against the reference binary. SPLIT and IGV stay high on DiversityGain at low cost weights to compound control-flow diversification across all 13 functions, including the trivial getters where cheap splits still change signatures. SUB and ICALL add arithmetic and call-site indirection to obscure the simple Point/Circle geometry math and virtual-ish dispatch, with ICALL's CorrectnessRisk kept moderate (0.3) since indirect calls through function pointers are the most fragile transform in C++ code with member calls. IBR is weighted for block-level randomization to break basic-block ordering comparison against the seed1 reference. All CorrectnessRisk weights remain low-to-moderate so the selector still applies passes to the largest functions where they are safest, preserving the round-1 correctness result while substantially raising transformation coverage.
